title: 06 · Community Behavior
text:
HN has a power-law karma distribution, dead hours, and a specific taxonomy of post types. Here we quantify the inequality, identify the structural patterns, and find the posts that generate debate without generating upvotes.
Show code

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from src.loader import db
from src.viz import set_style, save

set_style()
con = db()
Show code
stories = con.execute("""
    SELECT
        title,
        score,
        comment_count,
        author,
        HOUR(posted_at) AS hour_utc,
        DAYOFWEEK(posted_at) AS dow,
        YEAR(posted_at) AS year
    FROM stories
    WHERE score IS NOT NULL AND year BETWEEN 2008 AND 2024
""").df()

title: 06 · Community Behavior
text:
Score inequality — Gini coefficient


Show code
def gini(arr: np.ndarray) -> float:
    arr = np.sort(arr)
    n = len(arr)
    return (2 * np.sum(np.arange(1, n + 1) * arr) / (n * arr.sum())) - (n + 1) / n

scores = stories['score'].dropna().values
g = gini(scores)
print(f'Gini coefficient of HN story scores: {g:.3f}')
print('(0 = perfect equality, 1 = one story gets all points)')

# Lorenz curve
sorted_scores = np.sort(scores)
cumulative_scores = np.cumsum(sorted_scores) / sorted_scores.sum()
n = len(sorted_scores)
cumulative_pop = np.arange(1, n + 1) / n

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 6))
ax.plot(cumulative_pop * 100, cumulative_scores * 100, color='#e8604c', linewidth=2, label=f'HN stories (Gini={g:.2f})')
ax.plot([0, 100], [0, 100], 'k--', linewidth=1, alpha=0.5, label='Perfect equality')
ax.fill_between(cumulative_pop * 100, cumulative_scores * 100, cumulative_pop * 100, alpha=0.15, color='#e8604c')
ax.set_title('Lorenz curve of HN story scores', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Cumulative % of stories (sorted by score)')
ax.set_ylabel('Cumulative % of total points')
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
save(fig, '../data/fig_lorenz.png')
plt.show()

top1_pct = np.percentile(scores, 99)
top1_share = scores[scores >= top1_pct].sum() / scores.sum() * 100
print(f'Top 1% of stories (score ≥ {top1_pct:.0f}) capture {top1_share:.1f}% of all points')

title: HackerMining
text:
Hacker News is the tech industry’s water cooler. Since 2006, millions of stories have been submitted, voted on, and discussed. The aggregate of those decisions is a real-time seismograph of what the industry cares about — and when.
This project mines the full public HN dataset (35M+ items via Google BigQuery) to answer questions that are hard to answer from the inside:

title: HackerMining
text:
The 7 Key Findings

Technology life cycles are shockingly short — most go from hype peak to noise in under 4 years
ChatGPT was a 10× discontinuity, not just a bump — the largest single-event spike in 18 years of data
The best time to post is Tuesday 10am UTC — weekend posts underperform by 30–40%
HN score inequality rivals wealth inequality — Gini > 0.8, top 1% get 40%+ of all points
GitHub replaced personal blogs as the default link target by 2018
AI stories now score 2× the baseline — the topic is an upvote signal independent of quality
~50 power users drive a disproportionate share of all viral content

section: Monthly AI story volume — the ChatGPT inflection
text:
Monthly AI story volume — the ChatGPT inflection


Show code
AI_TERMS = {
    'Machine Learning': [r'machine learning', r'\bml\b'],
    'Deep Learning': ['deep learning', 'neural network'],
    'GPT / OpenAI': [r'\bgpt\b', 'openai', 'gpt-4', 'gpt-3'],
    'ChatGPT': ['chatgpt'],
    'LLM': [r'\bllm\b', 'large language model'],
}

for label, patterns in AI_TERMS.items():
    stories[label] = stories['title'].apply(lambda t: keyword_hits(str(t), patterns))

monthly_totals = stories.groupby('month').size().rename('total')

fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(AI_TERMS), 1, figsize=(14, 12), sharex=True)
chatgpt_date = pd.Timestamp('2022-11-01')

for ax, (label, _) in zip(axes, AI_TERMS.items()):
    monthly = stories.groupby('month')[label].sum()
    share = (monthly / monthly_totals * 1000).fillna(0)
    ax.fill_between(share.index, share.values, alpha=0.4, color='#e8604c')
    ax.plot(share.index, share.values, color='#e8604c', linewidth=1.5)
    ax.axvline(chatgpt_date, color='black', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5, linewidth=1)
    ax.set_ylabel(f'{label}\n(per 1k stories)', fontsize=8)
    ax.set_yticks([])

axes[0].set_title('AI discourse on Hacker News (2012–2024)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[-1].xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter('%Y'))
fig.text(0.92, 0.5, '← ChatGPT launch', va='center', rotation=90, fontsize=9, color='gray')
plt.tight_layout()
save(fig, '../data/fig_ai_discourse.png')
plt.show()

title: 07 · Key Findings
07 · Key Findings
section: Finding 1 — Technology life cycles are shockingly short
text:
Finding 1 — Technology life cycles are shockingly short
The hype heatmap shows that most technologies go from birth to peak to irrelevance in 3–5 years on HN. Blockchain peaked in 2018 and is now at background noise. Heroku flatlines after 2022. ChatGPT’s spike in 2023 is the single largest one-year jump in the dataset.


Show code
show('fig_hype_heatmap.png', 'Technology hype cycles 2007–2024')


↑ Technology hype cycles 2007–2024

title: 07 · Key Findings
text:
Finding 2 — ChatGPT was a 10× discontinuity
Every previous AI milestone (AlphaGo, GPT-3, DALL-E) caused a bump. ChatGPT caused a step-change. In November 2022, AI-related stories went from ~3% of front-page content to ~18% almost overnight — and never fully came back down.


Show code
show('fig_ai_discourse.png', 'AI discourse monthly, 2012–2024')


↑ AI discourse monthly, 2012–2024

title: 07 · Key Findings
section: Finding 3 — The best time to post is Tuesday 10am UTC
text:
Finding 3 — The best time to post is Tuesday 10am UTC
Weekend and late-night posts underperform by 30–40% in median score. The scoring sweet spot is weekday mornings in US Eastern time (UTC-5), when the most active voters are just starting their day.


Show code
show('fig_timing_heatmap.png', 'Median score by day × hour')


↑ Median score by day × hour

title: 07 · Key Findings
section: Finding 4 — HN score inequality rivals wealth inequality
text:
Finding 4 — HN score inequality rivals wealth inequality
The Gini coefficient of story scores is above 0.8 — comparable to national wealth inequality in the most unequal countries. The top 1% of stories capture more than 40% of all upvotes ever cast.


Show code
show('fig_lorenz.png', 'Lorenz curve of HN story scores')


↑ Lorenz curve of HN story scores

title: 07 · Key Findings
section: Finding 5 — GitHub replaced personal blogs as the default link target
text:
Finding 5 — GitHub replaced personal blogs as the default link target
In 2010, the top domains were personal .com and .org blogs. By 2018, github.com was the single most linked domain. Show HN posts almost exclusively link to GitHub — it became the de-facto portfolio site for the HN audience.


Show code

↑ Domain share over time

title: 07 · Key Findings
section: Finding 6 — AI stories score 2× higher than average since 2023
text:
Finding 6 — AI stories score 2× higher than average since 2023
Before 2020 there was no significant score premium for AI-related stories. By 2023–2024 the median AI story scores roughly double the non-AI baseline — meaning the topic itself is now a significant upvote signal, independent of quality.


Show code
show('fig_ai_score_premium.png', 'Score premium of AI stories')


↑ Score premium of AI stories

title: 07 · Key Findings
section: Finding 7 — A 50-user network drives a disproportionate share of viral content
text:
Finding 7 — A 50-user network drives a disproportionate share of viral content
The top 50 submitters by high-score post count have each posted 10–50+ stories scoring above 200. HN’s front page is significantly shaped by a small, recurring set of curators — not random submissions.

stories = con.execute("""
    SELECT
        title,
        url,
        score,
        comment_count,
        posted_at,
        HOUR(posted_at)    AS hour_utc,
        DAYOFWEEK(posted_at) AS dow,   -- 0=Sunday in DuckDB
        YEAR(posted_at)    AS year
    FROM stories
    WHERE score IS NOT NULL
      AND year BETWEEN 2010 AND 2024
""").df()

stories = title_features(stories)
